name: German sailor (soldier_GER_sailor)
about: Made by Tools/battle_units/soldier_sailors.py on soldier.py. Metres; x forward, y right, z up. Paints: 0 tunic, 1 trousers, 2 boots, 3 lower, 4 straps, 5 helmet, 6 pack, 7 skin, 8 wood, 9 steel, 10 coat, 11 coat_dark, 12 leather, 13 blanket, 14 hoof, 41 kapok, 42 shirt_own, 43 trousers_own, 44 hat, 45 ties (the eyes are painted as boots). near = LOD0, mid = LOD1, far = LOD2, all in the rest pose (arms 45 degrees down). Each point rides on bone `part` and, by `w2` (0 to 0.5), on bone `part2`. Skinning: a bone's turn G = G_parent * q (q from the clip, identity at rest; G of a bone with no track is its parent's), its head X = X_parent + G_parent * (head - head_parent + move), and a point p on it goes to X + G * (p - head). Quaternions are [t, w, x, y, z] in these axes (as Unreal's FQuat). Clips are in place: `stride` is the metres one loop covers; the game moves the unit. A mesh may carry `shade` per point (0 to 1, the wear and seam darkening): its colour is the paint's colour times shade; with no `shade` every point is 1. The German sailor: soldier.py's man (the same 32 bones) as a rating of the Navy at his action station, with no badge or insignia anywhere: a dark blue pullover with its stand collar and dark blue trousers, black leather shoes, the round flat cap with its two black ribbons hanging behind (no tally on its band), and a grey-green canvas kapok life jacket tied over the pullover. He carries no weapon (every clip's weapon is none). His colours are the file's own paints (new_paints, colours: kapok = the life jacket, shirt_own = the pullover, trousers_own, hat = the cap and its ribbons, ties = the jacket's ties), not an army's; colour_variants gives the white drill working dress of summer and the Mediterranean, the grey-green working dress, and the gun crew's steel helmet. Clips on deck from the motion capture; over the side and in the water keyed on his rig, the root at the sea's surface (water block). Also keyed on his rig, on deck: hands_up (surrendering) and a deck gun's crew, gun_layer, gun_trainer, gun_loader and ammo_passer (water: gun_crew).

idle.about: On deck, at ease, arms free (motion capture).

walk.about: On deck, walking (motion capture), arms free.

run.about: On deck, running (motion capture), arms free: to his station, or for the side.

cower.about: On deck, hunched, hands up by his head, as aircraft come in or the ship is hit (motion capture).

die_back.about: Killed on deck, falling back (motion capture); he stays where he falls.

die_forward.about: Killed on deck, falling forward (motion capture); he stays where he falls.

tread.about: Treading water upright in his vest, head and shoulders out: the legs in an eggbeater under him, the hands sculling at the surface, looking about.

wave.about: In the water, waving for rescue: kicking harder to rise (the pelvis 5 cm higher than treading), the left hand sculling, the right arm up over his head waving side to side twice a loop, the hand open, looking up and ahead.

swim_breast.about: Breaststroke, head up: the body near level just under the surface (the vest's back awash), a stroke of the arms (out, down, in under the chin, shot forward), the frog kick, the glide.

float_dead.about: Dead, floating face down, limp: the back and the vest awash, the head and arms hanging down in the water, the legs a little lower, rocked by the swell.

cling.about: Clinging to wreckage: both forearms over a floating spar ahead of him (`rail`: a round spar 0.16 m thick along his left-right, its middle 0.24 m ahead of the root and 0.06 m over the surface), hands hanging over its far side, the head down on his arms now and then, the body and legs hanging under it, a slow kick.

rail.about: the floating spar or wreck rail his arms lie over: a round bar along his left-right (the game's y), its middle here in the root's frame; draw any wreckage there

climb_net.about: Climbing a scrambling net up the ship's side: in place, the net upright 0.30 m ahead of his root, the root where his feet would stand; each loop he climbs `climb` metres (the game moves him up the net at climb / long metres a second). Right hand and left foot, then left hand and right foot.

fall_loop.about: Falling feet first through the air, in place (the game moves him on his fall): the root under his feet as if he stood; arms crossed over the vest, legs together, toes pointed, chin down. For a drop the jump clips do not cover.

jump_feet_first.about: Over the side from a deck 4 m over the water (the root at the sea's surface under the deck's edge; at the start his feet are on the deck, 4 m up): arms cross over the vest, a step off the edge, the fall (0.90 s), the splash as his feet reach the water (1.52 s, event `splash`), down to his feet about 2.1 m under, and up again into tread's first pose; he ends `end` ahead of the root (then play tread there).

jump_feet_first_2m.about: Over the side from a deck 2 m over the water (the root at the sea's surface under the deck's edge; at the start his feet are on the deck, 2 m up): arms cross over the vest, a step off the edge, the fall (0.63 s), the splash as his feet reach the water (1.25 s, event `splash`), down to his feet about 1.6 m under, and up again into tread's first pose; he ends `end` ahead of the root (then play tread there).

jump_feet_first_8m.about: Over the side from a deck 8 m over the water (the root at the sea's surface under the deck's edge; at the start his feet are on the deck, 8 m up): arms cross over the vest, a step off the edge, the fall (1.27 s), the splash as his feet reach the water (1.89 s, event `splash`), down to his feet about 2.8 m under, and up again into tread's first pose; he ends `end` ahead of the root (then play tread there).

enter_water.about: From the splash on (after fall_loop): his feet at the surface coming down at the speed of a 4 m drop, under, and up into tread's first pose; the root at the surface where his feet went in.

row.about: Pulling an oar in a boat, sat on the thwart (the root on its top, facing the stern as rowers do; his feet on the boards 0.35 m lower): the catch leaning forward with his arms out, the drive leaning back and the hands to the chest, the recovery. Both hands on one oar's loom; the `oar` track gives its handle and its rowlock (on his right) so the boat's oar can be drawn through them.

oar.about: the oar's handle (between his hands) through the stroke, and its rowlock (fixed, on his right), in the root's frame, the game's axes: draw the oar from the handle through the rowlock and on, its blade in the water at the catch (event oar_catch)

sit_raft.about: Sat on a raft's deck or a boat's bottom boards (the root on it), knees up, arms round his shins, hunched; he lifts his head and looks about, and lowers it again.

run_b.from: motion capture: run_styles.py's run_b (CMU 09_02 frames 21-111), with this file's own free arms from his run, the feet planted on his legs

run_c.from: motion capture: run_styles.py's run_c (CMU 16_36 frames 12-106), with this file's own free arms from his run, the feet planted on his legs

run_d.from: motion capture: run_styles.py's run_d (CMU 09_03 frames 10-101), with this file's own free arms from his run, the feet planted on his legs

hands_up.about: Surrendering, standing (on a deck or a surfaced boat's casing; the root under his feet): both hands raised open above his head, the palms forward; a slow small sway from foot to foot, the head turning a little as he watches. For the crew of a boat that gives up.

gun_layer.about: A deck gun's layer, at the gun's left side (the gun on his right): braced and crouched a little, his eye at the sight, both hands on the elevating handwheel ahead of him, turning it to and fro as the boat rolls. The `wheel` block gives the wheel's hub, rim and turn, and `sight` where his eye is, in the root's frame, so the gun's wheel and eyepiece can be put there.

wheel.about: the handwheel he turns: its hub here, upright across his front (its axis along x, toward him), his hands on its rim either side; turn it by `turn` (degrees, + his right hand up)

sight.about: where his eyes are (the mean between them; they move this little): put the sight's eyepiece just ahead of it, along x

gun_trainer.about: A deck gun's trainer, at the gun's right side (the gun on his left): the layer's stance mirrored, his eye at his own sight, both hands on the training handwheel ahead of him, turning it in longer sweeps. `wheel` and `sight` as gun_layer's.

wheel.about: the handwheel he turns: its hub here, upright across his front (its axis along x, toward him), his hands on its rim either side; turn it by `turn` (degrees, + his right hand up)

sight.about: where his eyes are (the mean between them; they move this little): put the sight's eyepiece just ahead of it, along x

gun_loader.about: A deck gun's loader, behind the breech: turned to his left he takes a round from the man behind him (ammo_passer), swings it round to his chest, lays it in the tray nose first and rams it home with his right fist, lunging after it; the breech closes and he turns back for the next, one round about every 5 s. The `round` block gives the round's base, its nose's way and when it is shown (in his hands, then sliding into the chamber), and the chamber's mouth, in the root's frame.

round.about: the round he loads: its base's middle (x, y, z) and its nose's way (dx, dy, dz) through the loop, drawn while shown (from the take until it is home in the chamber); `breech` is the chamber's mouth and `bore` the barrel's line, in the root's frame: put the gun's breech there

ammo_passer.about: Handing the rounds up through a hatch behind a deck gun: stood on a rung 0.9 m under the deck (the root at the hatch's middle on the deck, facing the gun's way), the deck at his waist, he holds a round up for the loader, lets it go as the loader takes it, stoops to take the next from below and lifts it up again, one about every 5 s. Played beside gun_loader from the same moment: `pair` gives the loader's root from his, so the round passes from hand to hand; `round` as the loader's.

round.about: the round he passes up, as gun_loader's (shown from when he lifts it from below until the loader takes it)

pair.about: the loader's root from his (the game's axes), both facing the same way, both clips played from the same moment: the round then passes from his hands to the loader's at t = 0.75 s

white_drill.about: the white drill working dress of summer and the Mediterranean: jumper and trousers (the cap stays dark)

grey_dress.about: the grey-green working dress worn later in the war

gun_crew.about: a gun crew's man: the same colours, with a steel helmet (a helmet finish, the flared helmet in dark grey 525A5E) drawn in place of the cap (helmet_paints)

water.sea_level: z = 0 in each water clip's root frame is the sea's surface (root `surface`)

roots.deck: the root on the deck under his feet, as the soldiers' clips
roots.surface: the root at the sea's surface (z = 0 is the water's top): place it on the water where he is; the pelvis_z below says how deep his pelvis rides
roots.feet: the root under his feet as if he stood (the fall: the game moves the root down his fall)
roots.net: the root where his feet would stand at the net's foot, the net hanging upright 0.30 m ahead of him; move the root up the net at climb / long metres a second
roots.seat: the root on the top of the thwart or the raft's deck he sits on, facing the clip's forward
roots.hatch: the root on the deck at the hatch's middle (he stands on a rung under it), facing the clip's forward

water.order: a man going over the side: run (or walk) to the rail, jump_feet_first (the 2 m, 4 m or 8 m one nearest the deck's height over the water; for any other height, fall_loop while the game drops him, then enter_water at the surface), then tread (or swim_breast, wave, cling); a body: float_dead. Picked up: climb_net up the side, or into a boat (row, sit_raft)
water.events: splash (splash_body: his feet into the water; height is the drop), surface (surface_gasp: his head out again), water_stroke and water_kick (swim_breast), net_grab (climb_net, the hand), oar_catch (row: the blade in), round_taken, ram and breech_close (gun_loader), round_up (ammo_passer); the deck clips' footsteps as the soldiers'
water.no_weapon: he has no weapon: the file has no weapon triangles; the weapon bone rides 2 m under his root in the water clips
water.gun_crew: on deck, keyed on his rig (the root on the deck under his feet): hands_up (surrendering, hands raised open above the head, a slow sway); a deck gun's crew: gun_layer (the gun's left, the elevating handwheel and the sight), gun_trainer (its right, the training handwheel, mirrored), gun_loader (takes a round from the passer on his left, lays it in the tray and rams it, about one every 5 s) and ammo_passer (in a hatch behind, the root at its middle: hands the rounds up, in step with the loader; `pair` gives the loader's root from his). Each clip's wheel, sight and round blocks say where the gun's parts go in its root's frame

about_wear: Wear and weather (Tools/battle_units/shade.py; Brian, 22 November 2026: uniforms dirtier the longer a unit is at the front, fresh replacements clean; rain darkens the cloth and splashes the mud higher; snow white on the shoulders and helmets). Per point, at near, mid and far and on each helmet finish's own mesh: `shade` (0.4 to 1) and `tint` (3 a point: red, green, blue) are the look as baked, a man some weeks in the line (wear W 0.6) in dry weather, for drawing paint x shade x tint as ever. `shade_clean`: the same shadow with no dirt (folds, under the straps, pack, belt and helmet brim, worn edges, the cloth's uneven fade). `dirt` (0 to 1): where dust and mud collect in dry weather (boots, leggings and trousers to a little over the knee in splashes, the knees, the seat, elbows, cuffs and hands, a little in the face's creases); `dirt_wet`: the same in rain (mud splashed up the thighs, caked boots, heavier knees and seat, the forearms and the front of the belly from going down in it). `wet` (0 to 1): how much the surface darkens when soaked (wool 1, webbing 0.8, leather 0.6, wood 0.45, helmet paint 0.3, steel 0.2, skin 0.15; less under the pack and the arms). `snow` (0 to 1): how much snow settles there on a man standing (open to the sky and facing up: the helmet's crown, shoulders, pack, the tops of the arms and boots; little on skin and steel). MIXING, per man: W = wear, from how long his unit has been at the front (0.1 a fresh replacement or a new unit, 1 six weeks or more in the line; replacements in a veteran unit stay low until they have been in it a while), R = rain (0 dry ground to 1 soaked) and S = snow (0 to 1), both from the battle's weather draw. In sRGB 0 to 1: base = paint x shade_clean x (1 - 0.35 x wet x R) (x the face's tone and tint); d = (dirt + (dirt_wet - dirt) x R) x W; soil = (DUST + (MUD - DUST) x R) x shade_clean, DUST (0.60, 0.54, 0.43) dry dust and dried mud, MUD (0.27, 0.21, 0.15) wet mud (or the field's own soil, lighter dry); colour = base + (soil - base) x 0.85 x d; then toward snow (0.92, 0.94, 0.97) x (0.6 + 0.4 x shade_clean) by 0.9 x snow x S. The gore paints (wound, bone, blood): shade 1, no dirt, wet or snow. Mid and far carry the near's, their shade eased off (90 % and 75 % of the darkening).

face_mesh.about: Close-range face (Tools/battle_units/face_mesh.py): the near mesh's face is split finer, red-green (no crack), and its new points set on MakeHuman's man the file was cut from (seed and nation below), so lids, lips, nostrils and the folds by the nose come back; the eyeballs' fronts are split once on their own spheres. No index moves: a split triangle keeps its place with its first piece; the other pieces and the new points are on the end of near's lists (from the first new point and triangle below), so helmet_tris and the gore ranges stay true. Each new point takes its parents' bone weights, shade, wear and tint, and in each face their move, facing and tint. Mid and far are as they were.

about_run_styles: run_styles.py (release 2, 23 November 2026): run_b, run_c, run_d and advance_b, advance_c, advance_d, each another runner's motion capture (CMU 09_02, 16_36, 09_03) with this file's own hold on his weapon; style_of names the clip each is a style of; the feet planted on this file's legs, the stride fitted to them (a planted foot slides no more than in his own run). The game gives each man one of the four (LandMen, the run-styles switch); far men banked in poses play the base clip's.
